quests.title: Witch's Revelation: Duty's Instruction

dialogue.t: Are you sure you can't make a copy of this card back for me?
Absolutely certain.
Hmm... It's very impressive. Maybe we could come to some sort of arrangement...?
Absolutely not.
Mm, I see. Obtaining beautiful card backs and playing powerful cards both require a certain price. I think I understand.

dialogue.sit: You came all this way to play cards?

dialogue.t: Hey! You don't know why Cyno's here! Maybe he came here to—
I sure did. That's my buddy, alright — we're on completely the same wavelength!
Seriously!?
There's a small gathering of TCG players taking place here in Fontaine. I heard participants get event-exclusive cardholders for free.
There were no pressing matters at the Akademiya, so I came over.
Even if there were pressing matters, Paimon has a sneaking suspicion you would have found a way to make them... not-so-pressing...
You're right! I managed to finish almost all of my work after only two weeks of overtime.
Sethos helped out, too, so I promised to bring him a cardholder for his trouble. He's very good at paperwork.
Well then, General Mahamatra, are you going to draw a card or not?
Of course. You say this card will predict my future, right?
Technically, not quite. But it's unlikely to cause much trouble if you choose to understand it that way.
Hm, I see. Is this like that line in "Duel Master"... "Stake your fate on the next card in the draw"?
And now it's my turn to draw...!

dialogue.sit: Cyno takes a deep breath, makes a stylish pose, and draws a card...

dialogue.t: Ah, reversed Temperance. A fitting card for the "General Mahamatra" of the Sumeru Akademiya.

dialogue.sit: You already know who Cyno is?

dialogue.t: Alice mentioned him a few times. She finds it funny that the stuffy old Akademiya has a General Mahamatra with such a "well-developed" sense of humor.
Please thank her for the compliment. Now that I've drawn a card, what should I do next?
Since it's reversed Temperance, or rather, reversed "Artistry," I suggest you maintain a state of doing nothing for the time being.
You've been acting rashly and have nearly lost your footing on the narrow bridge of fate.
It's because I've been playing too much cards, isn't it? Sethos and Tighnari told me the same thing — I've already adjusted my schedule.
...I'm not talking about playing cards. I mean your working hours. Surely Genius Invokation TCG isn't the only thing that demands the General Mahamatra's full attention?
My duties don't leave me much room to adjust them...
You're used to bearing the pressure of such a busy schedule alone?
There are other matras. We share the pressure among us.
But they all rely on you? Not just the matras, but the researchers and the people of Sumeru... So many people put their faith in you, General Mahamatra.
They never tell you, perhaps they don't even realize it themselves... Why would they, when they're all so captivated by your unstoppable wit?
But you can feel their gazes, looking to you night and day... Oh, and the shadow that walks beside you. He, too, is one of your burdens.
You're used to leading the way, carrying the burdens of others... I think, perhaps, this is the reason for your imbalance.
I have many friends. One of them just happens to be a "genius" who goes by the name of "Invokation TCG"...
So, it seems you have no intention of resting?
There's no time to rest.
Indeed. For someone such as yourself, if the inner battle is endless, then even death won't mark the end of duty.
Take this Lunar Arcanum. Perhaps it will lead you to the reason that restores your balance.
When it does, the battle within you should also reach a decisive end.
Thank you, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.
And my thanks to you as well. And don't worry, I promise I won't start acting too crazy.
...Huh? Why would you... Wait, was that...

dialogue.sit: He's come up with another one.

dialogue.t: ...What does this have to do with acting crazy?
Because now I have this card...
...People might accuse me of being a bona-fide "Lunar-tic"!

quests.description: You encounter Cyno at Barbeloth’s fortune-telling booth…
